verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Method: Figures are the %R values printed in the section 3.6 text (page 5), converted as 100 minus %R; Figure 5 is a heat map without printed numbers and Supplementary Table 2 was not available. Citrobacter and Proteus were described only qualitatively and are not included. Carbapenem susceptibility of the subset (0% by definition) is not shown. Carbapenem-resistance denominators: A. baumannii 388/808, K. pneumoniae 733/1897, P. aeruginosa 290/1199, Proteus 126/522 (24.1%), E. coli 433/3577, Citrobacter 37/356 (10.39%).

notes: A 2025 Frontiers in Medicine study of 8,359 non-duplicate Gram-negative isolates at SRM Medical College Hospital, Kattankulathur, Chennai, July 2022 to July 2024, tested by VITEK 2; 2,007 (24%) were carbapenem-resistant. Every figure shown is for the carbapenem-resistant isolates alone (E. coli 433, K. pneumoniae 733, P. aeruginosa 290, A. baumannii 388), so the figures are far lower than a general antibiogram would show and must not be read as the hospital's overall susceptibility. The paper prints % resistant, so figures are 100 minus %R and intermediate counts as susceptible. Only the few drugs quoted with numbers in the text are available. Carbapenem resistance was 48% in A. baumannii, 38.6% in K. pneumoniae, 24.18% in P. aeruginosa and 12.1% in E. coli.
